title: Subword Tokenization
motto: Word tokenizers choke on unseen words. Character tokenizers blow up sequence length. Subword tokenizers split the difference. Every modern LLM ships on one.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Word tokenizers choke on unseen words. Character tokenizers blow up sequence length. Subword tokenizers split the difference. Every modern LLM ships on one.

steps.title: The problem
cards: Your vocabulary has 50,000 words. A user types "untokenizable". Your tokenizer returns `[UNK]`. The model now has no signal about the word. Worse: the 90th-percentile document in your corpus has 40 rare words, which means 40 bits of dropped information per document.

Subword tokenization solves this. Common words stay single tokens. Rare words decompose into meaningful pieces: `untokenizable` → `un`, `token`, `izable`. Training data covers everything because any string is ultimately a sequence of bytes.

Every frontier LLM in 2026 ships on one of three algorithms (BPE, Unigram, WordPiece), wrapped in one of three libraries (tiktoken, SentencePiece, HF Tokenizers). You cannot ship a language model without picking one.
